source_type: Publicly reposted raster images, not a directly hosted original PDF from the competition organizer.
attribution: The search-index snapshot of the historical Fan olimpiadalari markazi (Uzbekistan Science Olympiad Center) public channel links directly to this Google Sites laboratory-paper page. The historical channel profile links to https://www.olympcenter.uz/. The Telegram handle is currently reused by a new channel and its old post is not currently accessible. Attribution therefore records the indexed historical announcement and does not treat the current channel owner as the source.
verification: All seven source images were visually reviewed. Physics pages identify the 2024 International Junior Science Olympiad Practical Examination, Physics, version Dec.9, and marking scheme. Their task identifiers and point values match the practical question packet. Chemistry pages carry the DEMO warning and match C_I 6.9 points and C_II 6.5 points, C_Table 1/2/3 and the phosphate titration. An organizer-hosted original key PDF has not been acquired.

sections.warning: Actual solutions are not provided in this order; this warning is retained prominently in Korean and English.

retrieval: Public HTTP only. Fresh public Google Sites HTML was requested with no-cache; newly issued image URLs then returned all seven images. No authentication, translation API, paid API or keys were used.
not_acquired: Separate official blank experiment answer sheets
source_notes: Physics E4 states a volume in cm³ but accepts a 16–18 g range. This source unit inconsistency is retained, including the g unit, rather than silently corrected.
Physics calibration scoring rows ±200 0.1p and ±300 0.2 are ambiguous in the source; the numerical rows are kept as native raster content.
Chemistry DEMO is a worked/example answer packet with reference values and marking guidance. Its remaining blank result fields do not make it a separate official blank answer book.
Chemistry retains the source expression V-bar = Y ± >0.4 mL and the original X/arrow observation convention. No mathematical reference values or order of solutions were invented.
